A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same robust LLM-unlearning study and contain 19 pages, including Appendices A-F. Their text, equations, figures and tables support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original WMDP and MUSE experiments, relearning and jailbreaking evaluations, and appendix ablations and generation examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendices B-F, including benchmark comparisons and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: The SAM-enhanced unlearning procedure, Algorithm A1, training objectives and RS, GP, CR and WA variants are unchanged. The landscape-loss definition correction does not establish a change to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use WMDP Bio, MUSE Books/News, Wikitext retention data, MMLU utility evaluation, AGNews/GSM8K/SST2 relearning sets and the same jailbreaking scenarios.

E2.justification: WMDP retains comparisons involving NPO, GradDiff and RMU with and without SAM, plus the same NPO smoothing variants. MUSE retains NPO versus NPO+SAM. Newly cited studies are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4, page 7, revises the stated landscape-evaluation loss from an average log-probability expression to cross-entropy next-token loss. This changes the documented evaluation quantity without establishing that experiments were rerun. Benchmark metrics, budgets and attack settings otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The same loss-landscape comparisons, attack-strength sweeps, RMU layer analysis, SAM-radius ablation and jailbreaking case studies remain. Their experimental evidence is unchanged, including Figures A1-A2 and Tables A3-A4.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 in both versions reports averaging relearning-attack performance over five independent random trials. Repeated-run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported values, plotted results and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains WMDP UE of 0.70 for NPO+SAM versus 0.57 for NPO under relearning with 20 samples and one epoch.

T1.justification: Page 7 replaces the average-log-probability formula, which lacks the minus sign required by its loss interpretation, with a cross-entropy definition. This is a limited mathematical-definition correction; the SAM derivations and Equations (1)-(12) remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same novelty claim connecting SAM to robust LLM unlearning and the same claims about resistance to relearning and jailbreaking attacks.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning smoother forget-loss landscapes, RMU's partial-parameter vulnerability, shallow-token behavior and SAM-radius tradeoffs are retained. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added or removed.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C retain the same implementation details, hyperparameter searches, training budgets and layer choices. The code-access information in the abstract is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Deeb and Roger (2024) and Lo et al. (2024) on unlearning vulnerabilities, and Jiang et al. (2023) on SAM. Research positioning otherwise remains stable. Consolidating Yao et al.'s preprint and publication entries does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: Changes are localized to the loss-description sentence, citation updates, duplicate-reference cleanup and the version/date stamp. The section order, contribution narrative and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The edits produce limited line-wrapping, spacing and bibliography page-break changes. Figures 1-6 and A1-A2, and Tables 1 and A1-A4, retain their displays, captions and placements.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves the sign-inconsistent landscape-loss definition on page 7 and acknowledges additional relevant prior work. These improve technical precision and attribution. The methods, experimental evidence and substantive interpretations remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
